# Known-red bench modules — the ratchet.
#
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# `make test-bench` became honest in 44fe689: a module that skips every test, or
# collects none, is now RED instead of printing OK. Five modules failed the moment
# the gate stopped lying. Demanding all five green before anything else may proceed
# would make the gate permanently red, and Makefile:9-11 already recorded what
# happens then — "a permanently red hook is one everybody bypasses with --no-verify."
#
# So the gate is red against a BASELINE, not against zero. Both directions are
# enforced by `make test-bench`:
#   - a module red that is NOT listed here      -> RED ("you broke something")
#   - a module listed here that now PASSES      -> RED ("delete its line")
# The set only tightens. Intention is not a mechanism.
#
# MEASURED 2026-08-16, and this pin is the whole validity of the file:
#   commit    main @ e8b44ea
#   command   make test-bench
#   scope     the 49 modules BENCH_TESTS derived on that commit
#
# The first version of this file said five. It was wrong, and the ratchet caught
# it on its first real run. "Red" had been extracted by grepping the output for
# FAILED, but the gate defines red as a non-zero exit OR zero coverage — and
# seven modules print "Ran N tests ... OK" and then exit non-zero anyway. Two
# definitions of the same word, one used to measure and the other to enforce.
# Re-measured by the gate's own definition: twelve, stable across two full runs
# on two different commits, so nothing regressed — the old number was simply
# blind. Take the baseline from the command that enforces it, never from a
# cheaper command that looks equivalent.
# Re-measure before trusting it on a different site or a later commit. A stale
# baseline is worse than no baseline: it reads as verified.
#
# The site pin below is PARSED, not prose. `make test-bench` compares it to
# $(TEST_SITE) and, when they differ, refuses to ratchet at all: it falls back to
# "every red is red". A baseline measured on one site says nothing about another,
# and a comment cannot stop anyone from ignoring that. Intention is not a
# mechanism — the whole point of this file.
#
#pin site=genesis-test.local
#
# Every entry MUST name a bead. A red with no bead is not known-red, it is ignored.
#
# format: <module>  <bead>  <cause>

# --- genuine test failures
test_approvals_integration           stabler-f74  errors=4; Reference No and Reference Date mandatory for Bank transaction
test_supplier_quotations_api         stabler-cd1  errors=1; fake stabler_settings cannot provide imports_supplier_groups_for
test_tender_flow_contract            stabler-vcq  failures=1; ':deal="null"' no longer present in the Vue source the contract greps

# --- asserted nothing
# stabler-56v (test_deploy_migrate_gate, collected-none) was paid off on 2026-08-20:
# the module declared a pytest-style bare class, which `bench run-tests` does not
# collect. It is now unittest.TestCase and asserts 7 guarantees about the deploy
# migrate gate.
test_related_documents_integration   stabler-97o  ZERO COVERAGE, skipped-3/3; site lacks the seeded fixture, prints OK (skipped=3)

# --- tests pass, the runner still exits non-zero
# stabler-5gc took six modules out of this block on 2026-08-16: they faked frappe
# into sys.modules and never handed it back, so frappe's own _cleanup_after_tests
# died on the fake. The ratchet is what surfaced them and would have demanded this
# deletion anyway -- a listed module that starts passing is itself RED.
# test_module_sandbox_hygiene now fails the build if a seventh one appears.
test_ci_transport_pi_link            stabler-slaa Ran 4 OK; teardown orjson decode error on empty input
